candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication actions, indications and medication-related client education
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — sitagliptin / DPP-4 inhibitor mechanism
candidate.educational_objective: Explain sitagliptin's DPP-4 inhibitor mechanism: prolonged incretin activity produces glucose-dependent increases in insulin and decreases in glucagon.

options.A: It inhibits DPP-4, increasing and prolonging active incretin hormones so insulin release increases and glucagon decreases in a glucose-dependent manner
options.B: It blocks renal SGLT2 transporters so glucose is excreted in the urine
options.C: It directly stimulates pancreatic insulin release independently of the incretin system
options.D: It delays intestinal carbohydrate digestion by inhibiting brush-border alpha-glucosidase enzymes

candidate.rationale: Current sitagliptin labeling states that the drug inhibits DPP-4 and slows the inactivation of incretin hormones such as GLP-1 and GIP. Increased active incretin levels increase insulin synthesis/release and reduce glucagon when blood glucose is normal or elevated. B describes an SGLT2 inhibitor mechanism, C resembles insulin-secretagogue therapy and omits the DPP-4/incretin mechanism, and D describes an alpha-glucosidase inhibitor. Therefore A is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Sitagliptin is a DPP-4 inhibitor that prolongs incretin activity, increasing insulin and reducing glucagon in a glucose-dependent manner.
candidate.source_locator: §12.1 Mechanism of Action: sitagliptin inhibits DPP-4, slows incretin inactivation, increases/prolongs GLP-1 and GIP action, and increases insulin release/decreases glucagon in a glucose-dependent manner
